newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Aluminium puts shine on Gencor profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Aluminium puts shine on Gencor profit.

text.p: Gencor Ltd on Tuesday announced a 74 percent jump in attributable income before exceptional items for the six months to end-December 1996, boosted by a strong performance from aluminium.
"I think there has been strong growth this half-year. Basically our earnings are up three-quarters in rands," Gencor chairman Brian Gilbertson told Reuters.
Pre-exceptional income totalled 1,018 million rand against 586 million in the year ago period. In dollar terms, earnings were up by 40 percent.
"The strongest surge has been in aluminium, principally because we bought in the total Alusaf. The earnings of (Alusaf) increased very strongly, nearly doubled," Gilbertson said in an interview.
Gencor last year increased its stake in Alusaf to 100 percent.
Gilbertson said Gencor's mineral sands operation Richards Bay Minerals (RBM) -- jointly owned with RTZ Corp Plc -- also contributed to the increase in profits.
And its platinum and coal interests in Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd and Ingwe Coal Corp Ltd also lifted profits.

The Witswatersrand gold interests contributed 69 million rand, an increase of 109 percent on the previous period, while the international gold division contributed 21 million rand against the 35 million in the six months to end-December 1996.
"An interesting feature this half-year which reverses the trend of the past is the very strong surge in earnings in South Africa.
"In this half-year, South Africa actually contributed 75 percent of our income where it was below 60 percent in the corresponding period a year ago," Gilbertson said.
Gencor said it expected second-half results to remain about the same as the first six months.
"If nothing goes wrong, I believe we would at least get similiar results in the second six months," Gilbertson said.
An important factor during the second half would be the performance of the rand and the price of aluminium, he said.
"You have to be cautious because the rand is very volatile...and the aluminium price is very important to us now, that took a knock a month ago but now has recovered very strongly," he said.
The company said net exceptional gains amounted to 861 million rand from 116 million rand in the six months to end-December 1995.
The exceptional items came from Gencor sales of assorted assets, mainly from the sale of its remaining 15.3 percent stake in industrial holding company Malbak Ltd last July.

Gencor said its new business and trading division produced trading income of 40 million rand against new business expenditure of 180 million rand -- 87 million rand more than in corresponding period in 1995.
"Various projects and opportunities are currently being evaluated so that increased expenditure is likely in the second half of the financial year," the company said.
